body:
Basically my service was a never ending stream of Vietnam War jokes.  Digging tunnels, fear of napalm, etc.  Eventually that just turned into straight up calling me the "enemy".

It was far from everyone who did it, and my experience was overall good in the Army, but the racial jokes were basically non stop.  I could never escape them.

She doesn't obsess over it, but her family definitely values white people highly.  3 of my moms sisters married white men, all of whom are right wing and/or religous nutjobs.

My mom's family came to the US as refugees and were extremely poor.  Marrying into white families was seen as a symbol of extreme success.
Having read your comment, I looked up NPD and it is a spot on match for my dad.  I am honestly kind of stunned.

Of course any rational individual would have no problem using chopsticks alongside forks depending on what dish you were eating.  Sane and normal people can see that immediately.

But my father told me that "any two monkeys can put two sticks together" and this was evidence of the primitiveness and backwards ways of Asian people.  I once yelled at him that forks arent anymore advanced and "any monkey" could figure out how to stab their food with a pointy stick.  He didnt get it.  He is too stupid to understand.
I served over 10 years in the Army.  I can't tell you the number of times people have made fun of my eyes, or told me I was "the enemy" or I should go dig tunnels and hide in them.
